# `sweep` (measureme) API Reference

The measurement layer: `lib/measureme`, imported as `import sweep`. A
`Station` collects QCoDeS parameters to follow, runs 0D–2D sweeps, and writes
each run to a directory (`data.tsv.gz` + `metadata.json`) via a `Writer`.

Source: `sweep/sweep.py`, `sweep/db.py`. `import sweep` re-exports the
`sweep.sweep` surface (`from .sweep import *`); `sweep.db`, `sweep.raster`,
`sweep.sweep_load` are submodules.

---

## Station

### `Station(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
A collection of followed parameters with sweep methods. `measurement_config`
is an arbitrary dict stamped into every run's `metadata.json` (channel→contact,
gains, bias, …). `basedir` is the run-directory root; falls back to the module
`BASEDIR` (see `set_basedir`) then `os.getcwd()`. The station writes `log.log`
into `basedir`, so the directory must exist before construction.

### `AsyncStation(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
Subclass of `Station`, same constructor and identical I/O / data layout. Reads
are parallelized per-instrument (one thread per distinct instrument, one
executor reused across a sweep), and same-instrument parameters are
batch-read when supported — SR830 `snap` (`SnapReadable`, ≤6 params) or
SR86x `get_values` (`BatchReadable`, ≤3 params), else sequential. Use this by
default; it produces byte-identical output to `Station`.

### `follow_param(param, gain=1.0)` → `Station` · alias **`fp`**
Append a QCoDeS parameter to the followed list. The stored column value is
**`param() / gain`** (gain division happens at read time). Returns the station,
so calls chain: `s.fp(sr0.X, gain).fp(sr0.P)`. For a true-current channel
follow it with `gain=1`. Column name is `param.full_name`.

### `add_comment(comment)`
Append a comment to `metadata['comments']`. **Comments are station-lifetime**:
every comment added since construction lands in every subsequent run's
metadata — rebuild (or otherwise reset) the station between runs of different
intent. `metadata['comments'][0]` is conventionally the recipe slug.

### `ramp(param, setpoint)`
Logged direct set — calls `param(setpoint)`. It does **not** sub-step; smooth
ramping is the driver's own `step`/`inter_delay` (or a driver `ramp_*` method).

### `register_run_before(fn, args)` / `register_run_after(fn, args)`
Register a hook called at each measured point. `args` must be a tuple. The hook
is called `fn(*args, **context)` where **context is injected by parameter
name** (via `inspect.signature` — the hook receives only the context keys it
declares):

| context key | available in | value |
|---|---|---|
| `station` | before & after | the `Station` |
| `writer` | before & after | the active `sweep.db.Writer` |
| `data` | after only | the most recent data row (list) |

A hook whose parameter is named `station` gets it from context — passing it in
`args` too double-binds (`TypeError: multiple values for 'station'`). Order any
`args`-supplied params before the context ones. Keyword-only hook params can't
be set positionally via `args`; bind them with `functools.partial` (signature
is seen through the partial, so injection still works).

### Other methods
- `measure()` → `SweepResult` — single 0D point.
- `watch(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` → `SweepResult` — repeat-measure over
  time until `max_duration` (or interrupt).
- `read(param, gain=1.0)` / `read_all()` — log a one-off read, no run written.
- `plot(x, y, z=None)` / `reset_plots()` — live monitor only, not the data.
- `reset()` — clear the interrupted flag so the station can sweep again.

---

## Sweeps

Each sweep method returns a `SweepResult` and writes one run directory. The
**data-row column layout** is fixed per method (and matches `metadata['columns']`).
`*followed` is the followed-parameter values in `fp` order, each already
gain-divided.

| method | signature | row layout |
|---|---|---|
| `measure` | `()` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `watch` | `(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `sweep` | `(param, setpoints, delay=0.0)` | `[time, setpoint, *followed]` |
| `multisweep` | `(params, setpointslist, delay=0.0)` | `[time, *setpoints, *followed]` |
| `megasweep` | `(slow_param, slow_v, fast_param, fast_v, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, slow, fast, *followed]` |
| `multimegasweep` | `(slow_params, slow_v_list, fast_params, fast_v_list, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, *slow, *fast, *followed]` |

- **`sweep`** — 1D. Sets `param` to each setpoint, waits `delay`, measures.
- **`multisweep`** — 1D, several parameters **co-swept**. `params` and
  `setpointslist` are parallel lists; `setpointslist[i]` is the vector for
  `params[i]`, and **all vectors must be equal length** (raises otherwise). At
  point j every `params[i]` is set to `setpointslist[i][j]` — one path through
  N-space, not a grid (e.g. a fixed-D (Vtg, Vbg) line).
- **`megasweep`** — 2D grid: outer `slow_param` over `slow_v`, inner
  `fast_param` over `fast_v`. `slow_delay` waits once per slow row (at the first
  fast point), `fast_delay` waits at every point.
- **`multimegasweep`** — 2D grid where each axis is a **co-swept bundle**.
  `slow_params`/`slow_v_list` and `fast_params`/`fast_v_list` are parallel
  lists; per-axis all vectors must be equal length. The grid is
  `len(slow_v) × len(fast_v)`; at each grid point every slow param and every
  fast param is set together. Example — field-slow, (Vtg, Vbg)-line-fast:
  `s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)`.
- **`init_delay`** (2D only) — `True` applies `slow_delay` before the very
  first point; `False` skips it (the axis is already parked there).

All sweeps are SIGINT-interruptible: an interrupt finishes the current point,
sets `metadata['interrupted'] = True`, and marks the station interrupted (call
`reset()` or rebuild before the next sweep).

### `SweepResult` (dataclass)
`SweepResult(basedir, id, metadata, datapath)` — the run root, the integer run
id, the final `metadata` dict, and the on-disk `data.tsv.gz` path.

---

## Module-level helpers (`sweep.*`)

- `set_basedir(path)` — set the global `BASEDIR` used when a `Station` is built
  without an explicit `basedir`.
- `list_measurements(basedir=None)` — render a markdown table of runs in a
  basedir.
- `measurement_info(i, basedir=None)` — print one run's metadata.
- `set_shutdown_handler(fn)` / `request_shutdown()` — register a
  ramp-to-safe callback and trigger graceful shutdown (thread-safe; if a sweep
  is active it stops after the current point, then calls `fn`). Used by the UPS
  monitor.

---

## Data on disk (`sweep.db`)

Each run is a directory `<basedir>/<id>/` with `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless TSV,
one row per point), `metadata.json`, and optional blobs (e.g. `plot.png`).

### `Writer(basedir, max_id=1_000_000, fsync_every=10)`
Creates the run directory at the lowest free integer id under `basedir`
(`.id`, `.dir`). `add_point(point)` / `add_points(points)` append rows
(fsynced every `fsync_every` points); `add_blob(name, bytes)` writes a sidecar
file (name may not be `data.tsv`/`data.tsv.gz`/`metadata.json`). `.metadata` is
a free dict saved to `metadata.json` on `close()`; on close the uncompressed
`data.tsv` is gzipped to `data.tsv.gz` (verified, then the plaintext removed).
Use as a context manager.

### `Reader(basedir, id)`
Reads a run back. `.metadata` (migrated to the current schema via
`migrate_metadata`), iteration yields rows of **strings** (no type conversion),
`all_data()` returns all rows, `blob(name)` reads a sidecar. `.datapath` is the
`data.tsv.gz` path. Use as a context manager. For numeric loads,
`np.loadtxt(reader.datapath, …)` or `hera.analysis.open_run`.

### Metadata keys written per sweep type
Common to all: `version`, `type` (`0D`/`1D`/`2D`), `function`, `columns`,
`comments`, `measurement_config`, `instruments`, `interrupted`, `start_time`,
`end_time`.

| function | additional keys |
|---|---|
| `sweep` | `param`, `setpoints`, `delay` |
| `multisweep` | `params`, `setpoints` (list of per-param vectors), `delay` |
| `megasweep` | `slow_param`, `fast_param`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `multimegasweep` | `slow_params`, `fast_params`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `watch` | `delay`, `max_duration` |

Two schemas coexist in older data — singular (`param`, `slow_param`) vs current
plural (`params`, `slow_params`). Read through `sweep.sweep_load` or
`hera.analysis.open_run`; don't hand-roll key access.

---

## Polygon rasters (`sweep.raster`)

Helpers for sweeping/plotting an arbitrary polygon region of a 2-D plane (e.g. a
bounded (Vtg, Vbg) window). A `multimegasweep` runs the rasterized point order;
these turn polygon vertices into that point list and back into a plot mesh.

### `rasterize(vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs, ys)`
The x/y coordinates of the grid points **inside** the polygon. `vertices` is
`(N, 2)`; `nx`/`ny` are grid points per axis over the bounding box; `fast_axis`
is 0 if x is the inner (fast) axis, 1 if y; `rev_x`/`rev_y` reverse a sweep
direction. Returns two 1-D arrays in raster order — feed them as the co-swept
fast/slow vectors of a `multimegasweep`.

### `pcolorize_data(zs, vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`
Bin measured values `zs` (in rasterized point order) back onto the regular
bounding mesh for `plt.pcolormesh(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`. Cells outside the
polygon are `NaN`. The `nx`/`ny`/`fast_axis`/`rev_*` arguments must match the
`rasterize` call that produced the sweep.

### `random_ngon_vertices(n)` → `(n, 2)` vertices
A random simple-ish n-gon, for tests/demos.
# `sharpelab_nb.drivers` API Reference

Instrument drivers in `src/sharpelab_nb/drivers/`, re-exported from the package:

```python
from sharpelab_nb.drivers import SRS_DC205, Yokogawa7651, ANC350
```

The `drivers` package (`src/drivers/`: `FastBi1K5`, `QSwitch`, `ContactMux`,
the VTI `SRS_DC205`, …) is documented separately in
[`drivers.md`](drivers.md).

---

## `SRS_DC205` — DC voltage source (fixed-duration ramp)

`SRS_DC205(name, address, *, ramp_num_points=100, ramp_wait_time=0.01, **kwargs)`.
Serial `VisaInstrument` (115200 baud).

| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voltage` | V | R/W | raw setpoint (7 dp) |
| `smart_voltage` | V | R/W | set → `ramp_voltage` |
| `voltage_range` | — | R/W | 0: ±1 V, 1: ±10 V, 2: ±100 V |
| `output` | 0/1 | R/W | output enable |

- **`ramp_voltage(volt)`** — software ramp from the current reading over
  `ramp_num_points` steps spaced `ramp_wait_time` apart (so the duration is
  roughly fixed regardless of ΔV), **plus a mandatory 10 s settle when
  `|Δvolt| > 0.1 V`**. (The VTI `drivers.SRS_DC205` of the same name uses
  rate-based (`ramp_rate` V/s) semantics and has no fixed settle — they are not
  interchangeable.)

---

## `Yokogawa7651` — programmable DC source (pre-SCPI, write-only cached)

`Yokogawa7651(name, address, *, coil_constant=None, **kwargs)`. The 7651 is
pre-SCPI (no `*IDN?`) and cannot report programmed values back over the bus, so
**all set parameters are write-only with a software cache**.

| parameter | unit | R/W | range / notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `volt` | V | W | ±30 V |
| `current` | A | W | ±0.12 A |
| `field` | T | W | requires `coil_constant=`; range = ±0.12·|coil| |
| `mode` | — | W | `'VOLT'` (F1;) / `'CURR'` (F5;) |
| `output` | bool | W | output enable |

- After a kernel restart the cache is empty, so the ramp methods raise unless
  the cache is seeded first: **`set_voltage_cache(value)`** /
  **`set_current_cache(value)`**, or pass `start=` to the ramp call.
- **`ramp_voltage(target, step=0.01, delay=0.05, start=None)`** /
  **`ramp_current(target, step=0.001, delay=0.05, start=None)`** — software ramp
  from the cached (or `start=`) value; `step` must be `> 0`.
- When `coil_constant` is given, `field.step`/`field.inter_delay` are
  pre-configured for safe ramping (0.1 mT / 0.1 s ⇒ ~1 mT/s).
- `trigger()` sends `E;` (normally automatic after each set). `get_idn()`
  returns a static dict.

---

## `ANC350` — attocube piezo motion controller (rotator)

`ANC350(name, dll_dir, *, device_no=0, num_axes=3, **kwargs)`. Loads
`anc350v2.dll`/`libusb0.dll` from `dll_dir`; exposes `num_axes` axes as a
`ChannelTuple` at `.axes` (each an `ANC350Axis`).

### `ANC350Axis` (one stepper axis)
| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | — | R | raw status int (decode via `is_moving`/`is_at_eot`/`has_sensor_error`/`is_sensor_disconnected`) |
| `position` | counts | R | raw sensor int32 (INT32_MAX when sensor power is off — the toploader default) |
| `rotation_count` | — | R | full-rotation counter |
| `amplitude` | mV | R/W | step drive amplitude, 0–70 000 |
| `frequency` | Hz | R/W | step frequency, 1–2000 |
| `dc_level` | mV | R/W | constant DC for fine positioning (output must be enabled) |
| `output_enabled` | bool | W | HV output; reads a software tri-state cache (True/False/None) — `set_output_cache()` to seed after restart |

Methods: `step(direction, count=1, *, wait=True, timeout=60.0, poll_interval=0.05)`
(±1 = forward/backward), `step_continuous(direction)`, `stop()`,
`wait_until_idle(…)`. `step`/`step_continuous` refuse to run unless the output
cache is `True`.

---

## Lock-in servo (`lockin_servo`)

Closed-loop positioning of an `ANC350Axis` against a lock-in voltage readback.
Not re-exported from the package — import from
`sharpelab_nb.drivers.lockin_servo`.

### `bring_up_servo_axis(name, axis, readback, *, amplitude_mv=60_000, frequency_hz=100, direction_sign=None, settle_time=0.5, v_min=-50e-3, v_max=+50e-3, tolerance=25e-6, max_iterations=200, step_count=1)` → `LockinServoedAxis`
One-call bring-up: set amplitude/frequency, enable HV output, resolve
`direction_sign` (if `None`, **physically steps the rotator** via
`calibrate_direction_sign` and prints the result to cache), and construct the
servo. `amplitude_mv` is millivolts (60 000 = 60 V).

### `LockinServoedAxis(name, *, axis, readback, direction_sign, v_min, v_max, tolerance=25e-6, settle_time=0.5, max_iterations=200, step_count=1)`
| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voltage` | V | R | one-shot read of the underlying readback |
| `target_voltage` | V | R/W | **set runs the servo loop synchronously**; get = last target (or None) |
| `last_iterations` | — | R | iterations used by the last run |
| `last_residual` | V | R | `abs(target − final)` of the last run |

`set` of `target_voltage` raises `ServoTimeout` if `max_iterations` is exceeded.
`abort()` requests the in-progress loop to stop (does not call `axis.stop()`).
`direction_sign` and `axis` are properties.

### `thermalized_setpoint(servo, readback_lockin, *, name=None, full_amp=None, off_amp=0.004, wait_s=60.0)` → `Parameter`
Wrap a servo move + sensor-excitation cool-down into one settable-only
`Parameter` (use as a sweep's slow axis): restore excitation → servo to target
→ drop excitation to `off_amp` → wait `wait_s` for the stage to thermalize.
After each set the lock-in amplitude is left at `off_amp`, so the followed
readback is noise during the read window — the meaningful axis is the setpoint.

### `calibrate_direction_sign(axis, readback, *, settle_time, noise_samples=5, noise_threshold=None, max_test_steps=10)` → `(sign, n_steps)`
Resolve step polarity empirically: issue forward steps until `readback` moves
past the noise threshold, return `+1` if it rose else `-1` (with the step count
used). `settle_time` is required. Called automatically by `bring_up_servo_axis`
when `direction_sign=None`.

# `sweep` (measureme) API Reference

The measurement layer: `lib/measureme`, imported as `import sweep`. A
`Station` collects QCoDeS parameters to follow, runs 0D–2D sweeps, and writes
each run to a directory (`data.tsv.gz` + `metadata.json`) via a `Writer`.

Source: `sweep/sweep.py`, `sweep/db.py`. `import sweep` re-exports the
`sweep.sweep` surface (`from .sweep import *`); `sweep.db`, `sweep.raster`,
`sweep.sweep_load` are submodules.

---

## Station

### `Station(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
A collection of followed parameters with sweep methods. `measurement_config`
is an arbitrary dict stamped into every run's `metadata.json` (channel→contact,
gains, bias, …). `basedir` is the run-directory root; falls back to the module
`BASEDIR` (see `set_basedir`) then `os.getcwd()`. The station writes `log.log`
into `basedir`, so the directory must exist before construction.

### `AsyncStation(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
Subclass of `Station`, same constructor and identical I/O / data layout. Reads
are parallelized per-instrument (one thread per distinct instrument, one
executor reused across a sweep), and same-instrument parameters are
batch-read when supported — SR830 `snap` (`SnapReadable`, ≤6 params) or
SR86x `get_values` (`BatchReadable`, ≤3 params), else sequential. Use this by
default; it produces byte-identical output to `Station`.

### `follow_param(param, gain=1.0)` → `Station` · alias **`fp`**
Append a QCoDeS parameter to the followed list. The stored column value is
**`param() / gain`** (gain division happens at read time). Returns the station,
so calls chain: `s.fp(sr0.X, gain).fp(sr0.P)`. For a true-current channel
follow it with `gain=1`. Column name is `param.full_name`.

### `add_comment(comment)`
Append a comment to `metadata['comments']`. **Comments are station-lifetime**:
every comment added since construction lands in every subsequent run's
metadata — rebuild (or otherwise reset) the station between runs of different
intent. `metadata['comments'][0]` is conventionally the recipe slug.

### `ramp(param, setpoint)`
Logged direct set — calls `param(setpoint)`. It does **not** sub-step; smooth
ramping is the driver's own `step`/`inter_delay` (or a driver `ramp_*` method).

### `register_run_before(fn, args)` / `register_run_after(fn, args)`
Register a hook called at each measured point. `args` must be a tuple. The hook
is called `fn(*args, **context)` where **context is injected by parameter
name** (via `inspect.signature` — the hook receives only the context keys it
declares):

| context key | available in | value |
|---|---|---|
| `station` | before & after | the `Station` |
| `writer` | before & after | the active `sweep.db.Writer` |
| `data` | after only | the most recent data row (list) |

A hook whose parameter is named `station` gets it from context — passing it in
`args` too double-binds (`TypeError: multiple values for 'station'`). Order any
`args`-supplied params before the context ones. Keyword-only hook params can't
be set positionally via `args`; bind them with `functools.partial` (signature
is seen through the partial, so injection still works).

### Other methods
- `measure()` → `SweepResult` — single 0D point.
- `watch(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` → `SweepResult` — repeat-measure over
  time until `max_duration` (or interrupt).
- `read(param, gain=1.0)` / `read_all()` — log a one-off read, no run written.
- `plot(x, y, z=None)` / `reset_plots()` — live monitor only, not the data.
- `reset()` — clear the interrupted flag so the station can sweep again.

---

## Sweeps

Each sweep method returns a `SweepResult` and writes one run directory. The
**data-row column layout** is fixed per method (and matches `metadata['columns']`).
`*followed` is the followed-parameter values in `fp` order, each already
gain-divided.

| method | signature | row layout |
|---|---|---|
| `measure` | `()` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `watch` | `(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `sweep` | `(param, setpoints, delay=0.0)` | `[time, setpoint, *followed]` |
| `multisweep` | `(params, setpointslist, delay=0.0)` | `[time, *setpoints, *followed]` |
| `megasweep` | `(slow_param, slow_v, fast_param, fast_v, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, slow, fast, *followed]` |
| `multimegasweep` | `(slow_params, slow_v_list, fast_params, fast_v_list, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, *slow, *fast, *followed]` |

- **`sweep`** — 1D. Sets `param` to each setpoint, waits `delay`, measures.
- **`multisweep`** — 1D, several parameters **co-swept**. `params` and
  `setpointslist` are parallel lists; `setpointslist[i]` is the vector for
  `params[i]`, and **all vectors must be equal length** (raises otherwise). At
  point j every `params[i]` is set to `setpointslist[i][j]` — one path through
  N-space, not a grid (e.g. a fixed-D (Vtg, Vbg) line).
- **`megasweep`** — 2D grid: outer `slow_param` over `slow_v`, inner
  `fast_param` over `fast_v`. `slow_delay` waits once per slow row (at the first
  fast point), `fast_delay` waits at every point.
- **`multimegasweep`** — 2D grid where each axis is a **co-swept bundle**.
  `slow_params`/`slow_v_list` and `fast_params`/`fast_v_list` are parallel
  lists; per-axis all vectors must be equal length. The grid is
  `len(slow_v) × len(fast_v)`; at each grid point every slow param and every
  fast param is set together. Example — field-slow, (Vtg, Vbg)-line-fast:
  `s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)`.
- **`init_delay`** (2D only) — `True` applies `slow_delay` before the very
  first point; `False` skips it (the axis is already parked there).

All sweeps are SIGINT-interruptible: an interrupt finishes the current point,
sets `metadata['interrupted'] = True`, and marks the station interrupted (call
`reset()` or rebuild before the next sweep).

### `SweepResult` (dataclass)
`SweepResult(basedir, id, metadata, datapath)` — the run root, the integer run
id, the final `metadata` dict, and the on-disk `data.tsv.gz` path.

---

## Module-level helpers (`sweep.*`)

- `set_basedir(path)` — set the global `BASEDIR` used when a `Station` is built
  without an explicit `basedir`.
- `list_measurements(basedir=None)` — render a markdown table of runs in a
  basedir.
- `measurement_info(i, basedir=None)` — print one run's metadata.
- `set_shutdown_handler(fn)` / `request_shutdown()` — register a
  ramp-to-safe callback and trigger graceful shutdown (thread-safe; if a sweep
  is active it stops after the current point, then calls `fn`). Used by the UPS
  monitor.

---

## Data on disk (`sweep.db`)

Each run is a directory `<basedir>/<id>/` with `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless TSV,
one row per point), `metadata.json`, and optional blobs (e.g. `plot.png`).

### `Writer(basedir, max_id=1_000_000, fsync_every=10)`
Creates the run directory at the lowest free integer id under `basedir`
(`.id`, `.dir`). `add_point(point)` / `add_points(points)` append rows
(fsynced every `fsync_every` points); `add_blob(name, bytes)` writes a sidecar
file (name may not be `data.tsv`/`data.tsv.gz`/`metadata.json`). `.metadata` is
a free dict saved to `metadata.json` on `close()`; on close the uncompressed
`data.tsv` is gzipped to `data.tsv.gz` (verified, then the plaintext removed).
Use as a context manager.

### `Reader(basedir, id)`
Reads a run back. `.metadata` (migrated to the current schema via
`migrate_metadata`), iteration yields rows of **strings** (no type conversion),
`all_data()` returns all rows, `blob(name)` reads a sidecar. `.datapath` is the
`data.tsv.gz` path. Use as a context manager. For numeric loads,
`np.loadtxt(reader.datapath, …)` or `hera.analysis.open_run`.

### Metadata keys written per sweep type
Common to all: `version`, `type` (`0D`/`1D`/`2D`), `function`, `columns`,
`comments`, `measurement_config`, `instruments`, `interrupted`, `start_time`,
`end_time`.

| function | additional keys |
|---|---|
| `sweep` | `param`, `setpoints`, `delay` |
| `multisweep` | `params`, `setpoints` (list of per-param vectors), `delay` |
| `megasweep` | `slow_param`, `fast_param`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `multimegasweep` | `slow_params`, `fast_params`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `watch` | `delay`, `max_duration` |

Two schemas coexist in older data — singular (`param`, `slow_param`) vs current
plural (`params`, `slow_params`). Read through `sweep.sweep_load` or
`hera.analysis.open_run`; don't hand-roll key access.

---

## Polygon rasters (`sweep.raster`)

Helpers for sweeping/plotting an arbitrary polygon region of a 2-D plane (e.g. a
bounded (Vtg, Vbg) window). A `multimegasweep` runs the rasterized point order;
these turn polygon vertices into that point list and back into a plot mesh.

### `rasterize(vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs, ys)`
The x/y coordinates of the grid points **inside** the polygon. `vertices` is
`(N, 2)`; `nx`/`ny` are grid points per axis over the bounding box; `fast_axis`
is 0 if x is the inner (fast) axis, 1 if y; `rev_x`/`rev_y` reverse a sweep
direction. Returns two 1-D arrays in raster order — feed them as the co-swept
fast/slow vectors of a `multimegasweep`.

### `pcolorize_data(zs, vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`
Bin measured values `zs` (in rasterized point order) back onto the regular
bounding mesh for `plt.pcolormesh(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`. Cells outside the
polygon are `NaN`. The `nx`/`ny`/`fast_axis`/`rev_*` arguments must match the
`rasterize` call that produced the sweep.

### `random_ngon_vertices(n)` → `(n, 2)` vertices
A random simple-ish n-gon, for tests/demos.
# `sharpelab_nb.drivers` API Reference

Instrument drivers in `src/sharpelab_nb/drivers/`, re-exported from the package:

```python
from sharpelab_nb.drivers import SRS_DC205, Yokogawa7651, ANC350
```

The `drivers` package (`src/drivers/`: `FastBi1K5`, `QSwitch`, `ContactMux`,
the VTI `SRS_DC205`, …) is documented separately in
[`drivers.md`](drivers.md).

---

## `SRS_DC205` — DC voltage source (fixed-duration ramp)

`SRS_DC205(name, address, *, ramp_num_points=100, ramp_wait_time=0.01, **kwargs)`.
Serial `VisaInstrument` (115200 baud).

| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voltage` | V | R/W | raw setpoint (7 dp) |
| `smart_voltage` | V | R/W | set → `ramp_voltage` |
| `voltage_range` | — | R/W | 0: ±1 V, 1: ±10 V, 2: ±100 V |
| `output` | 0/1 | R/W | output enable |

- **`ramp_voltage(volt)`** — software ramp from the current reading over
  `ramp_num_points` steps spaced `ramp_wait_time` apart (so the duration is
  roughly fixed regardless of ΔV), **plus a mandatory 10 s settle when
  `|Δvolt| > 0.1 V`**. (The VTI `drivers.SRS_DC205` of the same name uses
  rate-based (`ramp_rate` V/s) semantics and has no fixed settle — they are not
  interchangeable.)

---

## `Yokogawa7651` — programmable DC source (pre-SCPI, write-only cached)

`Yokogawa7651(name, address, *, coil_constant=None, **kwargs)`. The 7651 is
pre-SCPI (no `*IDN?`) and cannot report programmed values back over the bus, so
**all set parameters are write-only with a software cache**.

| parameter | unit | R/W | range / notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `volt` | V | W | ±30 V |
| `current` | A | W | ±0.12 A |
| `field` | T | W | requires `coil_constant=`; range = ±0.12·|coil| |
| `mode` | — | W | `'VOLT'` (F1;) / `'CURR'` (F5;) |
| `output` | bool | W | output enable |

- After a kernel restart the cache is empty, so the ramp methods raise unless
  the cache is seeded first: **`set_voltage_cache(value)`** /
  **`set_current_cache(value)`**, or pass `start=` to the ramp call.
- **`ramp_voltage(target, step=0.01, delay=0.05, start=None)`** /
  **`ramp_current(target, step=0.001, delay=0.05, start=None)`** — software ramp
  from the cached (or `start=`) value; `step` must be `> 0`.
- When `coil_constant` is given, `field.step`/`field.inter_delay` are
  pre-configured for safe ramping (0.1 mT / 0.1 s ⇒ ~1 mT/s).
- `trigger()` sends `E;` (normally automatic after each set). `get_idn()`
  returns a static dict.

---

## `ANC350` — attocube piezo motion controller (rotator)

`ANC350(name, dll_dir, *, device_no=0, num_axes=3, **kwargs)`. Loads
`anc350v2.dll`/`libusb0.dll` from `dll_dir`; exposes `num_axes` axes as a
`ChannelTuple` at `.axes` (each an `ANC350Axis`).

### `ANC350Axis` (one stepper axis)
| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | — | R | raw status int (decode via `is_moving`/`is_at_eot`/`has_sensor_error`/`is_sensor_disconnected`) |
| `position` | counts | R | raw sensor int32 (INT32_MAX when sensor power is off — the toploader default) |
| `rotation_count` | — | R | full-rotation counter |
| `amplitude` | mV | R/W | step drive amplitude, 0–70 000 |
| `frequency` | Hz | R/W | step frequency, 1–2000 |
| `dc_level` | mV | R/W | constant DC for fine positioning (output must be enabled) |
| `output_enabled` | bool | W | HV output; reads a software tri-state cache (True/False/None) — `set_output_cache()` to seed after restart |

Methods: `step(direction, count=1, *, wait=True, timeout=60.0, poll_interval=0.05)`
(±1 = forward/backward), `step_continuous(direction)`, `stop()`,
`wait_until_idle(…)`. `step`/`step_continuous` refuse to run unless the output
cache is `True`.

---

## Lock-in servo (`lockin_servo`)

Closed-loop positioning of an `ANC350Axis` against a lock-in voltage readback.
Not re-exported from the package — import from
`sharpelab_nb.drivers.lockin_servo`.

### `bring_up_servo_axis(name, axis, readback, *, amplitude_mv=60_000, frequency_hz=100, direction_sign=None, settle_time=0.5, v_min=-50e-3, v_max=+50e-3, tolerance=25e-6, max_iterations=200, step_count=1)` → `LockinServoedAxis`
One-call bring-up: set amplitude/frequency, enable HV output, resolve
`direction_sign` (if `None`, **physically steps the rotator** via
`calibrate_direction_sign` and prints the result to cache), and construct the
servo. `amplitude_mv` is millivolts (60 000 = 60 V).

### `LockinServoedAxis(name, *, axis, readback, direction_sign, v_min, v_max, tolerance=25e-6, settle_time=0.5, max_iterations=200, step_count=1)`
| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voltage` | V | R | one-shot read of the underlying readback |
| `target_voltage` | V | R/W | **set runs the servo loop synchronously**; get = last target (or None) |
| `last_iterations` | — | R | iterations used by the last run |
| `last_residual` | V | R | `abs(target − final)` of the last run |

`set` of `target_voltage` raises `ServoTimeout` if `max_iterations` is exceeded.
`abort()` requests the in-progress loop to stop (does not call `axis.stop()`).
`direction_sign` and `axis` are properties.

### `thermalized_setpoint(servo, readback_lockin, *, name=None, full_amp=None, off_amp=0.004, wait_s=60.0)` → `Parameter`
Wrap a servo move + sensor-excitation cool-down into one settable-only
`Parameter` (use as a sweep's slow axis): restore excitation → servo to target
→ drop excitation to `off_amp` → wait `wait_s` for the stage to thermalize.
After each set the lock-in amplitude is left at `off_amp`, so the followed
readback is noise during the read window — the meaningful axis is the setpoint.

### `calibrate_direction_sign(axis, readback, *, settle_time, noise_samples=5, noise_threshold=None, max_test_steps=10)` → `(sign, n_steps)`
Resolve step polarity empirically: issue forward steps until `readback` moves
past the noise threshold, return `+1` if it rose else `-1` (with the step count
used). `settle_time` is required. Called automatically by `bring_up_servo_axis`
when `direction_sign=None`.

## HERA — Step 3: SdH spot check, electron side (`sdh-spot-check`), n = +3.2×10¹² at D = 0, B 0 → 10 T

Calibration from run 5 (ana): c_bg/c_tg = 0.773 (data), c_tg = 2.796 mF/m² (9.5 nm prior), n_offset −0.089×10¹², D_offset −0.013 V/nm (R_CNP(D) symmetry). The D = 0 line inside the validators spans n = −1.27 … +3.27×10¹², so the electron side is the high-|n| side: spot at **n = +3.2×10¹²** → (V_tg, V_bg) = (+0.984, +1.166) V, 16 mV under the TG limit. **Feasibility (Step 2, model table):** F_L = 33.1 T; ABAB pair ≈ 7.5 / 25.6 T (m* 0.028 / 0.061 mₑ), ABCA singleton 33.1 T (m* 0.074); the heavy-ABAB-vs-ABCA split is 7.5 T. Grid: uniform in B (blocking magnet) — 50 mT from 0 to 1 T (MR background only; LK at T_e ≈ 8 K kills m* = 0.06 below ~1.5 T), **10 mT from 1 to 10 T**; 921 points. Dwell: `delay = 0` — each `magnet.field` set blocks through the ramp plus the driver's 3 s settle = 10 τ at τ = 0.3 s / 24 dB, i.e. the lock-in is at the settling floor at every point. Sensitivity fixed at 50 µV (5 kΩ FS): R(B = 0) ≈ 70 Ω is 1.4 % of range, but there is no SdH below ~1.5 T and the MR + SdH maxima at high B need the headroom; the FFT window starts above onset. **Price:** 10 T bare traverse 73 min + 921 × ~3.8 s per-point overhead (settle 3 s + reads) ≈ 58 min → **≈ 2 h 15 m**, ending at **10 T with the gates at the spot** — the hole-side spot check (n = −1.2×10¹²) then rides the magnet down 10 → 0.3 T, never re-traversing. Checkpoints: first 20 points (signal, sensitivity, leakage, field readback tracking setpoints); at ~3 T and ~6 T a partial FFT on the landed record (onset, tone count) — abort if the channel rails or no oscillation content has appeared by 6 T with R flat (then the fan is pointless at this T_e and the read is resolution-limited).

## HERA — Step 3b: SdH spot check, hole side (`sdh-spot-check`), n = −1.2×10¹² at D = 0, riding the magnet 10 → 0.3 T

Run 6 (electron, n = +3.2×10¹²) ends at 10 T with the gates at the spot. The investigation takes both signs (no side prior); the hole side of the D = 0 line reaches only n = −1.27×10¹² (TG −0.3 V limit), so the spot sits at **n = −1.2×10¹²** → (V_tg, V_bg) = (−0.280, −0.463) V. Feasibility (model): F_L = 12.4 T; ABAB pair ≈ 5.3 / 7.1 T (the near-CNP semimetal regime, tones close and balanced — the recipe's stated low-|n| exception), ABCA 12.4 T with m* ≈ 1 mₑ — LK-dead at this rig's T_e ≈ 8 K. **Coverage trade, stated:** this is a cheap preview, not a decisive read — it costs ~35 min over the bare 10 → 0 T ramp the session needs anyway, and a null here is resolvability-limited, not evidence. Grid: 20 mT uniform in B descending, 486 pts, delay 0 (3 s driver settle = 10 τ). Sensitivity 50 µV (5 kΩ FS; R(B = 0) ≈ 250–300 Ω this close to the CNP, MR headroom). Price: 9.7 T traverse 71 min + 486 × ~3.8 s ≈ 31 min → **≈ 1 h 45 m**, ending at 0.3 T. Checkpoints: first 20 points (rail? the CNP side at 10 T could be large), then the ana read at the end together with run 6.

Sensitivity fixed at 50 µV (5 kΩ FS): R(B = 0) ≈ 70 Ω is 1.4 % of range, but there is no SdH below ~1.5 T and the MR + SdH maxima at high B need the headroom; the FFT window starts above onset. **Price:** 10 T bare traverse 73 min + 921 × ~3.8 s per-point overhead (settle 3 s + reads) ≈ 58 min → **≈ 2 h 15 m**, ending at **10 T with the gates at the spot** — the hole-side spot check (n = −1.2×10¹²) then rides the magnet down 10 → 0.3 T, never re-traversing. Checkpoints: first 20 points (signal, sensitivity, leakage, field readback tracking setpoints); at ~3 T and ~6 T a partial FFT on the landed record (onset, tone count) — abort if the channel rails or no oscillation content has appeared by 6 T with R flat (then the fan is pointless at this T_e and the read is resolution-limited).

## HERA — Step 3b: SdH spot check, hole side (`sdh-spot-check`), n = −1.2×10¹² at D = 0, riding the magnet 10 → 0.3 T

Run 6 (electron, n = +3.2×10¹²) ends at 10 T with the gates at the spot. The investigation takes both signs (no side prior); the hole side of the D = 0 line reaches only n = −1.27×10¹² (TG −0.3 V limit), so the spot sits at **n = −1.2×10¹²** → (V_tg, V_bg) = (−0.280, −0.463) V. Feasibility (model): F_L = 12.4 T; ABAB pair ≈ 5.3 / 7.1 T (the near-CNP semimetal regime, tones close and balanced — the recipe's stated low-|n| exception), ABCA 12.4 T with m* ≈ 1 mₑ — LK-dead at this rig's T_e ≈ 8 K. **Coverage trade, stated:** this is a cheap preview, not a decisive read — it costs ~35 min over the bare 10 → 0 T ramp the session needs anyway, and a null here is resolvability-limited, not evidence. Grid: 20 mT uniform in B descending, 486 pts, delay 0 (3 s driver settle = 10 τ). Sensitivity 50 µV (5 kΩ FS; R(B = 0) ≈ 250–300 Ω this close to the CNP, MR headroom). Price: 9.7 T traverse 71 min + 486 × ~3.8 s ≈ 31 min → **≈ 1 h 45 m**, ending at 0.3 T. Checkpoints: first 20 points (rail? the CNP side at 10 T could be large), then the ana read at the end together with run 6.

import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg"); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pathlib import Path
from hera.analysis import open_run, resolve_channels, sdh_fft, sdh_onset, summarize_run, luttinger_frequency
D = Path("data")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 8))
for k, (rid, n12) in enumerate([(6, 3.2), (7, -1.2)]):
    r = open_run(D / str(rid)); print(summarize_run(r))
    ch = {c.cid: c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
    B = r.col("magnet_field"); I = r.col("sr0_X") / ch["sr0"].gain
    R = np.abs((r.col("sr1_X") / ch["sr1"].gain) / I)
    o = np.argsort(B); B, R, I = B[o], R[o], I[o]
    FL = float(luttinger_frequency(abs(n12) * 1e16))
    print(f"run {rid}: n={n12}e12 F_L={FL:.1f} T; R(0)={R[B<0.1].mean():.1f} R(max)={R.max():.1f} at {B[R.argmax()]:.2f} T; I {I.min()*1e9:.2f}-{I.max()*1e9:.2f} nA; "
          f"Itg {r.col('k_2400_tg_curr').min()*1e12:.0f}..{r.col('k_2400_tg_curr').max()*1e12:.0f} pA, Ibg {r.col('k_2400_bg_curr').min()*1e12:.0f}..{r.col('k_2400_bg_curr').max()*1e12:.0f} pA; T {r.col('T_sample').min():.3f}-{r.col('T_sample').max():.3f}")
    ax[0, k].plot(B, R, lw=0.8); ax[0, k].set_title(f"run {rid} raw, n={n12}e12"); ax[0, k].set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax[0, k].set_ylabel("Rxx (Ohm)")
    try:
        on = sdh_onset(R, B, r_full_scale=50e-6 / 10e-9)
        print(on.summary())
        blo = max(on.onset_b, 1.0)
    except Exception as e:
        print("onset err", e); blo = 2.0
    for lo in sorted({blo, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0}):
        for deg in (3, 5):
            f, sp = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(lo, 10.0), nfft=4096, bg_degree=deg)
            sp = sp[0]; m = f > 2
            pk = np.argsort(sp[m])[::-1]
            from scipy.signal import find_peaks
            pp, _ = find_peaks(sp[m], prominence=0.1 * sp[m].max())
            top = sorted(pp, key=lambda p: -sp[m][p])[:5]
            print(f"  FFT B[{lo:.2f},10] deg{deg}: res {1/(1/lo-1/10):.2f} T; peaks " + ", ".join(f"{f[m][p]:.1f}T({sp[m][p]/sp[m].max():.2f})" for p in top) + f"  [F/F_L: " + ", ".join(f"{f[m][p]/FL:.2f}" for p in top) + "]")
    f, sp = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(max(blo, 1.5), 10.0), nfft=4096, bg_degree=5)
    ax[1, k].plot(f, sp[0]); ax[1, k].axvline(FL, color="r", ls="--", label=f"F_L={FL:.1f}"); ax[1, k].set_xlim(0, 60); ax[1, k].legend(); ax[1, k].set_xlabel("F (T)")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/spots_67.png", dpi=90)
EOF

"""Runs 6-7 — sdh-spot-check at D = 0 (run-5 cal): raw Rxx(B) first, then FFT in 1/B and the Rxx-minima filling ladder."""
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
from hera.analysis import resolve_channels, sdh_onset

spots = [(6, +3.2), (7, -1.2)]          # (run, n in 1e12 cm^-2 on the geometry-prior scale)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(16, 8))
ladder = {}
for k, (rid, n12) in enumerate(spots):
    r = run(rid); ch = {c.cid: c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
    B = r.col("magnet_field"); I = r.col("sr0_X") / ch["sr0"].gain
    R = np.abs((r.col("sr1_X") / ch["sr1"].gain) / I); o = np.argsort(B); B, R = B[o], R[o]
    FL = float(luttinger_frequency(abs(n12) * 1e16))
    print(f"run {rid}: n = {n12:+.1f}e12 (prior scale), F_L(prior) = {FL:.1f} T; R {R.min():.1f}-{R.max():.1f} Ohm; "
          f"I {I.min()*1e9:.2f}-{I.max()*1e9:.2f} nA; |I_tg|max {np.abs(r.col('k_2400_tg_curr')).max()*1e12:.0f} pA, "
          f"|I_bg|max {np.abs(r.col('k_2400_bg_curr')).max()*1e12:.0f} pA; T {r.col('T_sample').min():.3f}-{r.col('T_sample').max():.3f} K")
    ax[k, 0].plot(B, R, lw=0.7); ax[k, 0].set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax[k, 0].set_ylabel("|Rxx| B_1-B_2 (Ohm)")
    ax[k, 0].set_title(f"run {rid} raw — n = {n12:+.1f}e12, D = 0")
    on = sdh_onset(R, B, r_full_scale=50e-6 / 10e-9); print(on.summary())
    f, sp = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(1.0, 10.0), nfft=4096, bg_degree=5); sp = sp[0]
    ax[k, 1].plot(f, sp / sp[f > 2].max()); ax[k, 1].axvline(FL, color="r", ls="--", label=f"F_L prior {FL:.1f} T")
    ax[k, 1].set_xlim(0, 60); ax[k, 1].set_xlabel("F (T)"); ax[k, 1].set_title(f"FFT in 1/B, B [1, 10] T (dF 1.1 T)"); ax[k, 1].legend()
    pk, _ = find_peaks(-gaussian_filter1d(R, 2), prominence=8, distance=5); pk = pk[B[pk] > 0.8]
    nuB = abs(n12) * 1e16 * cst.h / cst.e
    ladder[rid] = (B[pk], nuB / B[pk], R[pk])
# filling ladder of run-6 minima: find the density-scale s that puts nu = s * nu_prior on multiples of 4
Bm, nup, Rm = ladder[6]
ss = np.arange(0.80, 1.05, 0.001); cost = [np.sqrt(np.mean((s * nup / 4 - np.round(s * nup / 4)) ** 2)) for s in ss]
s_best = ss[int(np.argmin(cost))]; nu_true = s_best * nup
print(f"\nrun 6 minima ladder: best density scale s = {s_best:.3f} (rms {min(cost)*4:.2f} in nu) -> F_L(true) = {s_best*33.1:.1f} T")
print("  B (T):  " + "  ".join(f"{b:5.2f}" for b in Bm)); print("  nu:     " + "  ".join(f"{v:5.1f}" for v in nu_true))
present = sorted(set(int(4 * round(v / 4)) for v in nu_true)); print(f"  4k minima present: {present}; missing in 16-80: {[v for v in range(16, 84, 4) if v not in present]}")
ax[0, 2].plot(nu_true, Rm, "o"); [ax[0, 2].axvline(v, color="0.85", lw=0.8) for v in range(4, 92, 4)]
ax[0, 2].set_xlabel(f"nu = {s_best:.3f} x nu_prior"); ax[0, 2].set_ylabel("R at minimum (Ohm)"); ax[0, 2].set_title("run 6 Rxx minima vs filling (grid: nu = 4k)")
ax[1, 2].plot(ss, np.array(cost) * 4); ax[1, 2].axvline(s_best, color="r", ls="--"); ax[1, 2].set_xlabel("density scale s"); ax[1, 2].set_ylabel("rms off 4k (nu)")
ax[1, 2].set_title("ladder fit — run 6")
fig.suptitle("vti-02 SdH spot checks, runs 6 (e) / 7 (h), D = 0, T = 1.17-1.29 K, 10 nA"); fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()

# vti-02 stacking call — plan (HERA, rewritten at handoff 2026-08-23 05:30)

Goal: ABAB vs ABCA vs ABCB, per measured contact pair. Only one pair is wired
(sr1 = B_1–B_2, T_0 → B_3), so there is one region to call, with a series-mosaic
confound (ridges A and B in run 5).

## Discriminators (model: chiral decomposition, γ0 + γ1, γ1 = 0.38 eV, v = 1e6 m/s)

| | bands at D = 0 | SdH tones at fixed n | light-tone fraction vs n | D response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ABAB | two BLG-like (λ = 1.618, 0.618) | F_l + F_h = F_L, both ∝ n | ≈ 0.25–0.30, ~flat (rises slowly with n) | CNP gap weak/moderate; R(D) = R(−D) (inversion) |
| ABCA | one J = 4 band (trigonal-warping pockets at low n only) | single F_L at n ≳ 1e12 | — (no light tone) | large D-gap at CNP; symmetric in ±D |
| ABCB | J = 3 + J = 1 (cubic + Dirac-like) | two tones, F_D small | small at low n, **grows with n** (∝ E^{4/3}) | polar: R(n, D) ≠ R(n, −D); CNP min off D = 0 |

LL-level signatures: ABAB shows periodic missing 4k minima (light/heavy LL
coincidences) and LL crossings in the fan. ABCA shows a regular 4k ladder at high n.
ABCB's Dirac band carries a π Berry phase (half-integer Landau-plot intercept).

## Steps

1. [done] Gate C liveness (runs 0–3). Pass.
2. [done] 0 T gatemap + calibration (run 5). Ratio 0.773, n_off −0.089, D_off −0.013 (R_CNP symmetry vertex); two parallel ridges (series region B, +0.43e12).
3. [done] SdH spot checks (runs 6 e / 7 h). Fan feasible. Electron side has a two-band signature (7.1 / 22.2 / 29.5 T, ladder scale s = 0.894, missing ν = 40, 52, 56, 68–76). ABAB lean.
4. **[next] Landau fan at D = 0**: B slow 1 → 10 T uniform in 1/B (82 rows, Nyquist 45 T, ΔF 1.1 T); n fast along D = 0, −1.25 … +3.25e12 prior (151 pts, 0.03e12). Establishes:
   (a) the absolute n scale from the ν-line slopes (replaces the prior c_tg);
   (b) the tone count and F_i(n) per column, the sum rule F_l + F_h = F_L, and the light fraction vs n (ABAB flat vs ABCB rising vs ABCA none);
   (c) the missing-minima / LL-crossing pattern across n;
   (d) the hole side and near-CNP structure.
   ≈ 5 h 45 m. Ends at 10 T.
5. Finite-D fan or ±D cut, riding the field down from 10 T. Tests the D-symmetry (ABCB polarity) and the D-gap size (ABCA) at the densities where step 4 is clean. Shape decided from step 4. Candidates: an (n, D) map at fixed B ≈ 8–10 T on the ride down, or a fan at D = ±0.1 V/nm (the ±D reach is TG-limited; compute the window).
6. T-dependence of SdH amplitude (LK masses) at one electron density, if step 4 leaves ABAB vs ABCB open. Mass ratio m_l/m_h ≈ 0.38 for ABAB; the Dirac m* in ABCB is ∝ √n_D and small.
7. Call → final ana cell (per-region verdict, evidence with run ids, hedges).
8. Close-out: return-to-initial.

## What would change my mind

- The fan shows a single tone = F_L at n ≳ 1.5e12 with a complete 4k ladder, and the 7 T tone was region-B or harmonic content → ABCA.
- The light fraction climbs strongly with n (e.g. ≲ 0.1 at 1e12 → ≳ 0.25 at 3e12), or the Landau-plot intercept of the light tone is at 1/2 → ABCB.
- Strong ±D asymmetry in step 5 → ABCB. A large D-gap (≫ kΩ at |D| ≈ 0.2) → ABCA-leaning (run 5 already shows R_CNP rising to 2.4 kΩ at D ≈ +0.25; this alone does not discriminate).
- Series region B dominating the tone content → hedge the per-region call.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 10 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 600000ms are capped to 600000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
